explain.say: Supplies to the space station are expensive to launch, so it recycles all it can. Air and water go round and round a loop, a tiny version of Earth's own cycles.

faq.q: How does the space station make oxygen?
faq.a: It splits water using electricity, a process called electrolysis. Each water molecule gives up its oxygen, which is released into the cabin, and its hydrogen.
asks: Where does oxygen on the ISS come from?

faq.a: Yes. The station's water system distils and filters urine, sweat and breath moisture until the water is cleaner than most tap water on Earth. Astronauts joke that today's coffee is yesterday's coffee.
asks: How do astronauts get water in space?

faq.q: How is carbon dioxide removed on the ISS?
faq.a: Fans push cabin air through beds of special materials that soak up carbon dioxide. It is then dumped into space or sent to a machine that reacts it with hydrogen to make water.
asks: What happens to the carbon dioxide astronauts breathe out?

faq.q: Why does the station need to recycle?
faq.a: Every kilogram launched to space costs thousands of dollars, and each astronaut uses several litres of water a day. Recycling means far fewer supply flights.
asks: Why not just send up more water?

faq.q: What happens if the recycling breaks?
faq.a: The station keeps spare oxygen tanks, stored water and chemical oxygen generators as back-ups, and cargo ships bring supplies. Crews can also repair the machines with spare parts.
asks: Could astronauts run out of air?

facts: In 2023 NASA reported the space station's life support recovers about 98 percent of the water brought aboard.
The space station's Sabatier system reacts carbon dioxide with hydrogen to make water and methane.

quiz.say: How does the space station turn water into oxygen?
quiz.why: Electrolysis uses electricity to split water molecules into oxygen and hydrogen.

wrong.1: Steam is still water, not oxygen.
wrong.2: Freezing turns water into ice, not oxygen.
